name: Brain store and maintenance
summary: Where memory lives and how it stays healthy: the brain store, migration, shared settings, storage, maintenance, health and hygiene.

features.name: Brain store and sync
features.summary: Append-only shared and private record partitions that several machines can sync, with device, partition and shard care.
capabilities: Appends JSON-line records to per-device monthly shards, so two machines never write the same file
Stamps each record with a hybrid logical clock and a sha256 of its body
Folds records by authority first, human over agent, then by clock
Spills bodies over the 16 KiB line cap into sha256-named blobs; a blob not yet synced reads as pending
Sends records of private or unjudgeable pages to the private partition; a machine without it refuses the write
Creates the store by `store init` (shared, private or both), `o2b init`, vault-less `brain init` or migration
Quarantines a corrupt shard line, or a blob missing for 7 days, on this machine only (`store shard`)
Returns record ids new since an index watermark, grouped by partition, stream, scope and topic (500, max 5000)
Drops a decommissioned device from roster and cohort by a permanent `shared` record (`store device retire`)
Clears this machine's state of a removed `private` partition; refuses `shared` (`store partition leave`)
limits: Does not sync files itself: an external file-sync tool must carry the store folder or each partition folder
No encryption at rest and no record signatures: the checksum detects damage, not forgery by a syncing peer
Shards are append-only and nothing compacts them, so removed records stay on every machine that holds them
`brain_changes` refuses below local reach (a remote MCP call) and returns no ids; the CLI always runs locally

features.name: Upgrades and store migration
features.summary: Moves a legacy brain into the store, upgrades release-owned files and relocates vault state, with dry runs.
capabilities: Migrates a legacy brain: quiesces writers, backs up and test-restores, converts in journaled passes, verifies
Starts the migration by itself after an update in a detached worker, unless `auto_store_migration: false`
Resumes a stopped migration without importing anything twice (`--resume`)
Restores the legacy tree and replays records with a legacy form (`--rollback`); the rest stay in the store
Moves the legacy tree to a local archive once every cohort device switched or retired (`--remove-legacy`)
Counts an unswitched cohort device silent for `migration.silent_device_days` (30, 0 off) as retired
Adds `_brain.yaml` keys, refreshes `_BRAIN.md`, fixes corrupted principles (`brain upgrade`), on updates too
Moves a store that 2.0.0 left outside the vault into `.open-second-brain-store/` by copy, verify, bind, commit
Inventories each declared vault state surface with its path and reachability (`state status`)
Moves vault state to `--to <dir>` under a sha256 manifest, verifying copies before deletes (`state migrate`)
limits: `store move-into-vault` never runs by itself and refuses while a session, dream pass or migration writes
`brain upgrade --apply` refuses on a machine switched to the store, which has no managed files to upgrade
`state rollback` restores only files whose digest still matches the manifest and names each changed file
A migration rollback works only until the legacy tree has left the vault

features.name: Shared brain settings
features.summary: Settings every machine of a brain agrees on, read and changed by name, with operator values protected from agents.
capabilities: Gets, lists, sets and unsets a shared setting by name (`<block>.<field>` or a scalar key) from the CLI or MCP
Once switched, writes a change as a `setting-set` or `setting-unset` record in `shared`'s `settings` stream
Folds each key as a register: human beats agent authority, then the later clock; unset restores the default
Pre-switch, edits the key in `Brain/_brain.yaml`; store-native keys (`view.language`) are always records
Refuses agent writes over a human value and to operator-only keys (integrity, read, capture scope)
Validates every value with the settings validator before it writes
Folds `brain.schema.*` lists per entry from `setting-entry` records, so edits on two machines both survive
Answers a device-only key with the machine config line that holds it
limits: Covers only keys every machine shares; device keys stay in each machine's config file, which it does not edit

features.name: Storage usage and compaction
features.summary: Per-surface storage census with a growth forecast against a cap, and compaction of expired receipt records.
capabilities: Measures bytes per surface (Brain tree, snapshots, archives, payloads, state, index); a refused one is named
Appends one `storage_usage` sample per report and fits a per-day linear trend over 30 days once 3 days exist
Tiers usage against `storage.cap_bytes`: warn at 80% or 30 days left, critical at 95% or 7; no cap: unbounded
Re-measures when deciding: ingest refuses at critical, the maintenance lane pauses at `storage.pause_percent`
Scans the continuity and metrics receipt ledgers for records older than 30 days (`brain receipts scan`)
Folds old records of named shards into one aggregate line per kind and month; previews unless `--apply`
Snapshots first, rewrites each shard atomically with compare-and-swap, logs a `receipt_compaction` record
limits: The census covers the vault's `Brain/` tree and index files, not the brain store folder
Below local reach the report is refused and no sample is taken; compaction runs at local reach only
Compacts only this device's shards named from a scan, and refuses to apply on a store-only machine

features.name: Scheduled maintenance
features.summary: A lease-guarded quiet-window lane that runs dream, reindex, links and custom tasks, or prints a cron recipe.
capabilities: Runs dream, reindex, bridges, clusters and relink, least recently succeeded first, journaling each
Gates a run on a local hour window, query rate (5 in 10 minutes), host run-queue pressure and storage tier
Holds an expiring 30-minute SQLite lease so two heavy passes never share a vault; `--force` never bypasses it
Refuses a task after `maintenance.failure_streak_limit` failures in a row (default 3); `--retry` passes one
Runs machine-config shell commands as `custom:<name>` tasks, off unless `maintenance_custom_tasks` is set
Keeps reindex keyword-only unless `maintenance_embeddings` is set, then prints predicted spend and records it
Previews relink anchor additions to signal pages and rewrites them only with `--relink-apply`
Shows the lease holder and the recent journal rows (`maintenance status`)
limits: Runs only when something calls it; it installs no schedule, and `--cron-template` only prints one
Custom tasks come from the machine config only, never from the vault or an MCP call, and record no spend

features.name: Brain health checks
features.summary: Invariant checks with safe repairs, semantic health, recovery probes and an operator status with next commands.
capabilities: Runs 66 registered read-only checks: frontmatter, status-vs-folder, ids, links, logs, store shards and clocks
Applies safe repairs (`doctor --repair --apply`): closes dangling dream workruns, prunes dead evidence links
Plans remediation (`--remediate`), applying only auto-safe steps (chmod hardening, hash re-stamp), capped
Reports contradictory preferences (Jaccard 0.5, opposite sign), uncovered concepts and claims stale 180 days
Gives an operator verdict of clean, watch or investigate (`brain summary`)
Combines doctor, health, hygiene, stale scan and review candidates in `brain status`, a command per problem
Probes config, folders and index (`watchdog`); remediation creates missing folders and replaces non-folders
Scores preferences on diversity, connectivity, orphans and gap pressure (`vitals`)
Hides concept-gap and batch-inflation findings older than `health.silence_before` (`brain health-baseline`)
Ranks top-N maintenance actions (10) from duplicates, stale pages, broken links, tokens (`brain actions`)
limits: Doctor writes nothing without `--repair --apply` or `--remediate`; repairs cover workrun gaps and dead links
Contradiction detection is token overlap with opposite sign; it uses no model
Below local reach, store findings are computed without the private partition

features.name: Memory hygiene
features.summary: Finds contested, duplicate, stale and unused memories and broken pages, and applies only the fixes chosen.
capabilities: Scans for contested truth slots, Jaccard 0.8 duplicates, stale pages, low use and url-only sources; no cosine
Applies only named finding ids: merge, supersede via `hygiene.resolver_cmd`, recompile, archive, retire
Reports preferences, signals and log days idle past `temporal:` thresholds (90, 30, 180 days) (`brain stale`)
Merges pages sharing a dedup key (`page-dedup --apply`) by stamping `merged_into` and repointing wikilinks
Fixes structural drift with `lint --consolidate --apply`
Recompiles derived pages whose sources changed (`brain refresh`)
Unions `private` into `visibility` for informal privacy markers (`privacy-marker-restamp`); dry run by default
Adds one Stop-hook line of finding counts per change (`hygiene-digest`), off unless `hygiene_digest_enabled`
Lints `--paths` or git-dirty pages read-only; errors exit 1, `--strict` warnings exit 2 (`brain validate`)
Checks index-detected identity-tier frontmatter drift, restores it (`--apply`) or accepts it (`brain tiers`)
limits: Scans are read-only, but `brain refresh --stale` and `brain tiers accept` write with no `--apply` flag
Contested slots resolve by themselves only through an operator-set `hygiene.resolver_cmd`; else they wait
The digest line reaches only hosts with a non-blocking Stop channel (Claude Code)
